headline: Oil prices rise amid escalation between US and Iran and oversupply fears
summary: Brent crude for January delivery gained 0.76% to $93.14 a barrel as US-Iran tensions escalated, while fears of excess supply weighed on the market.
why: Brent is the main international benchmark for crude oil, and it reflects shifts in Middle East supply risk and global demand.
why_moved: Prices gained amid escalation between the US and Iran, although fears of oversupply limited the rise.
original_headline: Precios del petróleo suben en medio de escalada entre EU e Irán y temores de exceso de oferta
